RAVINDER DUDEJA, J.
1.

This is a petition under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, seeking quashing of FIR No. 0315/2021, dated16.12.2021, registered at P.S Hauz Quazi Delhi under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC and all proceedings emanating therefrom on the basis of settlement between the parties.
2.

The factual matrix giving rise to the instant case is that the marriage between Petitioner No.1 and Respondent no. 2/complainant was solemnized on 10.07.2019 as per Hindu Rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
No Child from the said wedlock.
However, on account of temperamental differences Petitioner No.1 and Respondent No. 2 are living separately since 06.12.2020.
3. As per averments made in the FIR, Respondent No. 2 was subjected to physical and mental harassment on account of dowry demands by the petitioners.

FIR No. 0315/2021 was lodged at the Kunal Sharma & Ors vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74256080/
1 instance of respondent no. 2 at PS Hauz Quazi under sections 498A/406/34IPC against the petitioners.

sentences.text: 4. During the course of proceedings, the parties amicably resolved their disputes before the Counselling Cell, Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi and the terms of settlement were written in the form of Settlement Deed dated 15.01.2025.

It is submitted that petitioner no.1 and respondent no. 2 have obtained divorce on 01.07.2025 and the petitioner no.1 has paid the entire settlement amount of Rs.
6,00,000/- (Rupees Six Lacs Only) along with the articles as per the list attached with the report to respondent no. 2 as per the schedule in the settlement.

Copy of the settlement deed dated 15.01.2025 has been annexed as Annexure P-7.
5.
Parties are physically present before the Court.
They have been identified by their respective counsels as well as by the Investigating Officer SI Dharmendra Kumar, from PS Haux Quazi.

6. Respondent No. 2 confirms that the matter has been amicably settled with the petitioners without any force, fear, coercion and she has received the entire settlement amount as also the gold and dowry articles and has no objection if the FIR No. 0315/2021 is quashed against the Petitioners.
7. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned Additional PP appearing for the State, also has no objection if the present FIR No. 0315/2021 is quashed.

8. Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable settlement of disputes in Rangappa Javoor vs The State Of Karnataka And Another, Diary No. 33313/2019, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 74,
Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. vs Babita Raghuvanshi &Anr., (2013) 4 SCC 58& in Gian Singh vs State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 9.

sentences.text: Further, it is settled that the inherent powers under section 482 of the Code are required to be exercised to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of any court.
Further, the High Court can quash non-compoundable offences after considering the nature of the offence and the amicable settlement between the concerned parties.
Supreme Court and this Court have repeatedly held that the cases arising out of matrimonial differences should be put to a quietus if the parties have reached an amicable settlement.

Reliance may be placed upon B.S. Joshi v. State of Haryana, (2003) 4 SCC.
10.

sentences.text: In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion, it would be in the interest of justice, to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.

11. In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 0315/2021, dated 16.12.2021,
registered at P.S Hauz Quazi Delhi under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC and all the other consequential proceeding emanating therefrom is hereby quashed.
12. Petition is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
